findings.title: Role-mapping checks lose manage/admin fallback
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only evaluate the corresponding fine-grained scope for the client. They do not fall back to canManage(client), unlike the V1 evaluator where an administrator who can manage a client (including via the manage-clients admin role) can map its roles. A full realm admin or a user granted only the Clients 'manage' scope is therefore incorrectly forbidden from role/composite/client-scope role mapping in V2.

findings.title: Resource display name is not resolved for Clients resources
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type: it returns 'All users' for the type resource and resolves instance resources to usernames. Clients resources fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), but instance resources created by getOrCreateResource are named by client id and have no display name set, and the 'Clients' type resource is not translated to 'All clients'. Permission/resource representations for Clients will consequently expose a null/blank name instead of the client id or 'All clients'.

findings.title: Missing all-clients resource causes NullPointerException during evaluation
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no instance resource exists the code loads the all-clients resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls findByResource(server, resource) and later builds a ResourcePermission from it without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the 'Clients' resource is absent (for example in realms whose admin-permissions client was initialized before the Clients type existed, since init() returns early when the client already exists and never adds the new scopes/resources). Permission checks for such realms then throw NullPointerException instead of denying permission or lazily creating the type resource.

findings.title: Removal listener can dispatch to V2 evaluator that throws on cleanup
findings.body: The listener now runs whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled, but management() dispatches to MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so when both features are enabled, role/client/group removal events invoke V2 cleanup and fail with UnsupportedOperationException instead of disabling permissions. The guard needs to exclude the V2 case (or the dispatch needs to use the V1 evaluator for this cleanup).
